interactions.summary: A student asks whether Virgil is complicit in imperial corruption because he wrote the poetry, and Jiang answers that Virgil remains only in limbo because Dante needs a slower awakening in which Virgil gradually becomes suspect.
The reading completes the violent river by naming more tyrants and highway predators, then closes the Nessus episode.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Student reading Dante aloud with Jiang transition

interactions.summary: Canto 13 opens with the black wood of the suicides and the harpies, then stages the shocking moment when a broken branch bleeds and speaks.

speaker_notes.note: Jiang's repeated ASR form 'Inead' refers to the Aeneid and is central to his claim that readers must be weaned off imperial Virgil.

claims.claim: Jiang says Virgil is implicated in the imperial corruption of poetry but remains only in limbo because Dante needs readers to arrive at that recognition gradually.
Jiang says Dante's journey is not only moral movement from sin to virtue but also an awakening from darkness into interpretive light.
The violent river narrows and shallows by degree while still holding named tyrants and predators such as Attila, showing punishment as proportioned depth rather than a single undifferentiated pool.
Canto 13 introduces the second ring of violence as a black, pathless wood inhabited by harpies and by human souls transformed into thorny trees.
Virgil tells the wounded tree that Dante hurt it only because the scene was too incredible to believe without physical proof.
claims.temporal_scope: Quoted explanation within the canto on 2026-06-23.

signature_moments.moment: Virgil is probably the villain, but Dante cannot reveal that all at once.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Virgil is probably the villain here
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang's sharpest reversal so far in the lecture and reorients the poem around interpretive deprogramming.

signature_moments.moment: The suicide wood becomes believable only when a branch bleeds and talks.
signature_moments.source_phrase: from that broken stump issued together both words and blood
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the packet's defining horror-image and marks a shift from political paradox to embodied metaphysics.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The beloved imperial text Jiang says Dante must lead readers away from through slow discovery.
The black forest of the suicides in the second ring of violence, populated by harpies and tree-souls.

chronology_notes.note: This packet finishes Jiang's Virgil/Augustus inversion and then pivots cleanly into the suicide wood of Canto 13.

uncertainty_notes.note: Several proper names in the list of tyrants are ASR-noisy, but the structural point about graded depth in the blood river remains clear.
